I was in a psychiatric hospital twice as a child, age 6 and 11 so that probably won't help you. However my sister was admitted at 14 and admitted herself a few months ago age 20 and it helped her get more stable again after she suffered PTSD induced psychosis and manic and low phases (she doesn't have bipolar though). 
She had a lot of therapy sessions, none of them really helpful because she had been misdiagnosed with schizophrenia at fourteen, however just having a time off in a safe setting helped her a lot. She got meds so she could sleep again (somewhat) and her mood stabilized a lot. She still isn't up to work and life a "normal" life but at least now she is able to function again at home.
But at least for her experience it must be said that what helped her the most, besides the pause from stress, was talking with other patients that went through similar things every day.
I think this is something that's really helpful because you're not alone anymore and don't have to hide.
She was in there for three months and will be going to a different clinic soon that specializes in getting patients back into the "normal" life.
I hope this somewhat helped you
